id: Serpent Dream / Marlēné Claudine Radice (AU) / Box Of Hammers-Pyramid Club, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Serpent Dream / Marlēné Claudine Radice (AU) / Box Of Hammers
long_description:
Serpent Dream is the duo of Kelda Morris and Dusty - an evolving project that explores the intersections between ambient, classical, folk and sound art to offer emotive experiences. They have a large repertoire of original music to draw from and curate their sets to suit the intended audience.

Kelda Morris is an accomplished violinist who trained classically in both Aotearoa and Austria, and has extensive orchestral experience. With an interest in Russian romantic style playing, and klezmer music, she has recently expanded her skillset to perform with various folk, ambient, experimental, postrock and metal bands, and also explores production and vocals.

Dusty is a self-taught musician and acoustic guitar player with roughly 10 years experience as composer, performer and producer. Their solo acoustic music has been described as serene, haunting, and trance-inducing. Dusty is known for their unique blend of finger-style guitar playing, melancholy tinged lyrics and atmospheric sound design, fusing these elements into unique and emotive audio journeys.

-

Marlēné Claudine Radice is an Australian composer who specialises in notated electroacoustic composition by exploring how art and sound compliment one another. Taking recorded sounds away from their original sources, they process and manipulate these into new musical structures. Raw industrial noises, looped voices and hypnotic soundscapes are layered to create a nuanced and original sound. Marlēné is a trained physical theatre performer and a passionate advocate for queer youth arts education and inclusive theatre practices. They are a lead facilitator for Rebus Theatre’s iDrama classes for adults with intellectual disabilities and have been a facilitator for their annual Acting Out: On Screen Queer youth holiday course since 2023. Outside of their work as a composer and teacher Marlēné has worked as a field recorder primarily specialising in archiving Indigenous Australian songlines. They are currently co-producer and music director for The Seeing Place; a contemporary theatre company they co-founded in 2023.

-

Box Of Hammers is the solo ambient project of John Kingston, based on painterly use of guitar tones and drones.

venue: St Peters Hall, Beach Rd, Paekakariki, Paekakariki, Wellington
long_description:
KA RONGO KOE KI TE WAIATA O TE KŌIWI? Can you hear the song of the bone?

Supported by Creative NZ - Gigi Crayford under 'HINE' presents the debut EP ‘KA MUA KA MURI’. A music journey tracing the threads of Whakapapa, exploring relationship to Atua, Pūrākau and the transformation of learning an ancestral tongue. Recorded on ancestrally affiliated land with full instrumentation by herself and her whānau, this project is drawn from deep wells of meaning and connection.

“GiGi’s soulful voice has an ancient quality, that feels whole and embodied. There is a depth that is rare and potent.” - Ariana Tikao, renowned practitioner and composer of taonga pūoro and an established writer and poet.

“Mesmerising, theatrical and soulful reo” - Toni Huata - Former director of SOUNZ, Singer, Composer and legendary Māori performer

‘KA MUA KA MURI EP’ weaves Taonga Pūoro, sonic storytelling, poetry and Gigi's original folk noir style in both English and Te Reo Māori. A singer-songwriter on Autoharp, Guitar and Piano, Gigi is supported by brother Miles Crayford on Organ, father Greg Crayford on drums, Charlie Budd on Taonga Pūoro and Aslan Rowlands on Electric Guitar.

This project brings echoes of the emotionally drenched lyricism of Joni Mitchell, the enigmatic voice akin to Kate Bush and soaring ecstatic moments echoing Pink Floyd. Interwoven with Taonga Pūoro; creating a contemporary genre-bending experience. HINE reverberates with authentic expression, wahine power & the vital place music has in healing & self discovery.

With her maiden single release and successful show at MĀORILAND ŌTAKI in 2024 for’ KA MUA KA MURI’ HINE explored the grief of living in a matrix paved over matriarch world and the journey of remembering to return to the earth from a human-centric culture.

This tour releases the final 4 songs of the EP. Each an ode to a different Atua Māreikura, ranging from Papatūānuku, Hine Te Iwa Iwa, Murirangawhenua, Hine Moana, Hine Raukatauri & Hine Takurua.

Shows in Tāmaki Makaurau Auckland, Paekākāriki, Pōneke Wellington and Ōhinehou Lyttelton.

name: Battle Of The Banjos
long_description:
Saturday 8th of August at Vogelmorn Upstairs is shaping up to be a five-string showdown between your favourite banjo-slinging bands. Each band brings remarkable talent and a unique sound, but only one lucky plucker will be crowned champion of Battle of the Banjos.

STAN ANTONIO - Phoebe and Alex grew up attending folk festivals and have played around Wellington as part of various folk groups. They dabble in the realms of Americana, folk, and bluegrass, and have recently been writing music together. Their influences include classic artists such as Gillian Welch and Dave Rawlings, more contemporary artists such as Adrianne Lenker. They aspire to use the banjo as a force for good in this world, alongside close harmonies and acoustic guitar.

SOUTHRIVER - Alt-folk band Southriver seek to draw you in with their banjo and mandolin led tunes, sweet harmonies and earnest lyrics. From the folk scene in Te Whanganui a Tara they travel the country from North to South finding friends along the way. Releasing their debut EP in 2025 under the banner of the Bidibids they have honed their sound to reflect their love of folk, bluegrass and americana.

With songwriter Sarah August on banjo and guitar and composer Brendan Schenk on mandolin and guitar, these two have been writing and playing together since 2021 creating a repertoire of troubled tunes for troubled times.

BANJO BEN AND THE BREEZE - Banjo Ben and The Breeze are a new folk comedy band based in Wellington. They're known for their iconic beanies and their theatrically charged gigs, which are packed full of catchy lyrics, wild stories and plenty of laughs. Also covering the fields of rap, techno, and pirate music, you'll learn to expect the unexpected. This group cannot be pinned to one specific genre, but their influence stems from artists such as The Decemberists, Flight of the Conchords and Billy Strings. Hold on to your hats because The Breeze is blowing into Vogelmorn…

BOTTOM BUNK CLUB - Bottom Bunk Club is a folkpunk/antifolk band from Pōneke. They combine the energy of a sweaty basement gig with the feel-good plucking and strumming of an old-time bluegrass hoedown. They sound like if Woody Guthrie grew up listening to lots of punk rock. Their melodies are infectious, and you'll be singing along whether you want to or not...


Note:
Vogelmorn Upstairs is not a wheelchair accessible building. There is an accessible bathroom in the space. This is an all ages venue but those under the age of 16 must be accompanied by a designated adult after 8pm. The Vogelmorn Precinct is a community space located in a residential area. With that in mind, the team ask that you be kind to others and that when you leave the gig, you do so quietly to avoid disturbing our neighbours. Please note that our restaurant is currently closed. We are temporarily arranging food trucks for events when possible. Toasties and pies are also available at the bar.

The Undercurrent presents The Kelburn Viaduct Municipal Ensemble Jug Band!

KVmeJB has been on the scene since 2013 when they played their lively set of jug band music for the Wellington Folk Festival. There have been a few line-up mixes along the way, here is the most recent formation!

Neil Worboys began performing in bands and composing songs in Wellington in the early ‘70s, and continued to play jug band and roots music in the 1980s and early 1990s while living in Gisborne. In 1995, he formed the Wellington Heads, a jazz / rhythm n’ blues band which also includes Bill Wood. Before coming to New Zealand Carol Bean was living in Los Angeles where she had the privilege of being a student of Ry Cooder’s. Her electric blues band Blue Highways played Wellington gigs for 10 years, at the Bristol, Bodega, the Sound Shell, San Fran, and the Martinborough Wine Festival.

Bill Wood plays a dobro, and adds backing vocals to the mix. Bill also has another life (but not as we know it) in the 3rd Octave Band. He is also a core member of the Wellington Heads. Baz Carter is a member of the 3CPo trio- now a foursome. He is a filmmaker, a guitarist, a bass player, a songwriter and owns a dog called Nina... Aotearoa / New Zealand adventurous music label iiii Records is very excited to release an epic double LP by shape shifting, tectonic plate lifting supergroup Farewell Spit.
Named after and recorded at Lyttleton’s iconic music festival Port Noise, with an additional track recorded at Wellington’s Meow, the album is destined to be an instant classic and a work which stands as utterly unique in the oeuvre of each of the band members’ catalogues – all of whom are prolific and iconic figures in New Zealand music.
Over four sides of the double LP Farewell Spit traverse vast territories of sculptured sound, noise and melodicism, always a cohesive whole whilst eschewing instrumental tropes of flamboyant technical bravado or noodling twaddle.

Here’s what NZ legend Bruce Russell of the Dead C has to say:

The expanded sextet Spit is almost that most preposterous of creatures, the Super Group. But it would be fairer to describe them simply as a dream team. What happens when the top shelf of Aotearoa jazz improvisers (Donaldson, Henderson) meets the supplest of rhythm sections (Gooch, Callwood)? Again, 'rhythm section' is almost an insult, these guys play all across the map; and over the edge. Then you throw in two wild card guitar-players, one from the ethno-musicological improv side of the street (Beban), the other a grown-up punk who can play free and choreographically (Carter) - and stand well clear. Listening to these four sides will answer all questions. Everyone does the unexpected: (Henderson's uncanny Abdullah Ibrahim pianisms are drawn from below the bottom of the probability deck) and we all go home barefoot... The highest compliment I can pay them is that I repeatedly fell asleep and half-awakened throughout the Port Noise set that comprises most of this double album -and I've slept in the front row of a solo Cecil Taylor gig. So for me, Farewell Spit are right-fucking-on.

Bruce Russell, Lyttelton.

long_description:
Petra Dubach & Mario van Horrik (Netherlands) have been an artistic duo since 1983, working from the notion that movement and sound are identical; without movement (vibration) nothing can be heard. They explore this idea in many forms through installations and performances using sound, image, new-media and technology, with a particular interest in projects that deal with communication, formal translations, and (mis)understanding. They have presented their work worldwide and join us on the back of their upcoming installation and performances at the Audio Foundation in Tāmaki Makaurau. For this concert they will be performing their Table Piece for amplified table. Travel made possible with the help of Dutch Cultural Foundation - the Constant van Renesse Fonds.

-

David Long & Amy Jean Barnett (duo)

David Long is a composer, performer, founding member of The Mutton Birds, and member of easy listening noise band, Teeth. His career has spanned over 40 years and seen him work on numerous projects to commercial and critical acclaim. In his own words he likes to mash shit up, creating orchestral scores that utilise not only classical instruments but all sorts of things. Among many accolades, this year he and Stephen Gallagher were jointly awarded an Emmy for Outstanding Music Direction and Composition for their work on TV series, Secrets at Red Rocks, and in 2020 he won best score at the APRA Silver Scrolls for the BBC drama series, The Luminaries.

Amy Jean Barnett is a composer and artist working with sound, performance, installation and acoustic ecology in her practice. Barnett's live performances weave intricate narratives through sound, drawing on electroacoustic techniques, minimalism, and field recordings. Working with recorded fragments, improvisation, and a tactile engagement with materials, she creates auditory environments of shifting textures that invite deep listening and reveal the subtle complexities of sound unfolding over time. Barnett is currently pursuing a Master of Musical Arts at the New Zealand School of Music under the supervision of Michael Norris.

Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

name: Ubuntu And Other Cultural Concepts Of Humanity
long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Ubuntu and other Cultural Concepts of Humanity!

The Ubuntu Cultural Conversation is an interactive and inclusive cultural event that explores how humanity is understood, expressed, preserved, and shared through diverse cultural perspectives. Through a combination of live music, poetry, storytelling, and open audience conversations, the event will create a space for meaningful dialogue, cultural exchange, reflection, and connection.

The programme will feature live musical performances by Ras Judah (Botswana), Mohamed Shemi (Tanzania), and friends, alongside poetry and opportunities for audience participation. Shared cultural food will further contribute to the spirit of hospitality, community, and connection that lies at the heart of Ubuntu.

The African concept of Ubuntu is often expressed through the powerful saying, “I am because we are.” Rather than placing individual achievement at the centre of social life, Ubuntu emphasises the importance of community, cooperation, reciprocity, and shared wellbeing. It encourages us to recognise the humanity in one another and to respond to the challenges faced by others with understanding, kindness, and support.

The philosophy of Ubuntu reminds us that our lives are enriched when we care for one another, celebrate our differences, and work collectively to create inclusive and connected communities. It offers an opportunity to reflect on what it means to be human and how our relationships with others shape the societies in which we live.

We are SO LUCKY to have Adam McGrath returning to Hilltop – he’s one of the best. Adam has already had a full-on year (and it’s only half way), including touring with the ‘Come Together’ Born To Run – Bruce Springsteen concerts, and then touring with Gary McCormick. Adam is the winner of the 2024 Aotearoa/New Zealand Folk Artist of the Year Award at the Aotearoa/New Zealand music awards. Described by RNZ as a “National Treasure” and the Herald as “NZ’s toughest minded songwriter”, Adam is also widely known as lead singer and songwriter with one of NZ’s most loved roots/country bands The Eastern. Adam’s new album Wrecker Songs was released on May Day 2026 to coincide with the 75th anniversary of the Maritime Union of New Zealand (MUNZ). It hit #1 – Aotearoa Albums Chart and #4 – Official Top 40 Albums (all albums, domestic and international). It also reached #1 on the IMNZ (Independent Music New Zealand) Album Chart. “Wrecker Songs is here, on all the streamers, the cd’s are here the vinyl is late, the spirit is high, the heart is a eye and its wide, the muscle is gristly, the bones brittle, the mind shows grit despite the fog, the fists clenched, the struggle real, the solidarity true.”… Click for the first song on the album -> ‘The Assembly” Adam is a folk singer and yarn spinner stationed, he says, wherever he can get a key! He spends eight months a year on the road between NZ, Australia, Europe and parts beyond. With The Eastern and solo he has shared stages with and opened for Fleetwood Mac, Steve Earle, Old Crow Medicine Show, Paul Kelly, Jimmy Barnes and many, more. His song Hope and Wire was the inspiration behind Gaylene Preston’s TV series of the same name and he is known for his service orientated approach to music in the years since. Described as “maybe part folk singer, part preacher, part boxer, and part rodeo clown he is however all heart”. Raucous, tender, roof and spirit raising, a McGrath show goes straight for the spirit level in all of us, looking deep for the good parts and hoping to reach all the thoughtful bits that matter.
Adam’s first solo album was released December ’23. “It’s called Dear Companions, because of everything I’ve learnt or am learning about the people in the songs and what they help me learn about myself and about the world big and small (especially small). But that kind of conception is just how records start, where they end up is up to whoever gets a copy in their life.”

name: Tudor Consort Presents Prophetiae Sibyllarum
long_description:
The Tudor Consort is thrilled to present Orlande de Lassus' Prophetiae Sibyllarum, one of the greatest works of the sixteenth century.


The twelve motets that comprise the work are written in a style known as ‘musica reservata’ or ‘musica secreta’, featuring highly chromatic chord progressions for greater emotive and expressive effect. In the very first bars Lassus breaks the rules of accepted harmonic practice to produce the sort of music that will not be written again for hundreds of years.


As the name suggests, this style of music was considered very specialised and just for performance to an educated and initiated audience. Prophetiae Sibyllarum is seen by many as the apex of this style, blending expressionism with breathtaking beauty.


This incredible work provided the basis of our sold out performance of Michael Norris’ SoundCathedral at the Aotearoa Festival of the Arts, and we can't wait to perform it in its entirety.


We round out the programme with our favourite Tudor works by Tallis, Byrd and Gibbons, alongside Ross Harris’ Vobiscum in aeternam which was written for The Tudor Consort in 2011.

River of Nihil have riffs, big choruses, the prog, the solos, the sax and now it will have Aotearoa New Zealand

long_description:
In their only Wellington show this year, Too Many Chiefs return to the excellent Vogelmorn Upstairs.

Mates on the road rolling out top quality songwriting and musicianship, with lashings of irony and
humour. - East Auckland Times
Three songwriters argue over headline billing, playing order, and whose shout it is, while talking
about themselves and playing their self-selected ’Greatest Hits’.
Wayne Mason is something of a Kiwi icon, having won the 'song of the Century' with his song
'Nature', first recorded in the '60s with The Fourmyula, and also covered by the Muttonbirds in the
'90s. Also a founder member of Rockinghorse and The Warratahs, Wayne now records and tours
under his own name. When on the road with the Chiefs his job is to deliver philosophical
profundities such as ‘music is like water - it just seeps away into the ground’.
Rob Joass is a 3 times Tui Award finalist, singer/songwriter and leader of folk/rock troubadours
Hobnail. His gritty songs are equal parts folk and country rock, with the occasional barb of satirical
humour betraying a cynical perspective on the human condition honed by decades of constant
touring through the highways and back roads Europe, Canada and NZ. Rob calls this ‘repeatedly
smashing myself up against a wall’.
Andrew London tours and records with his own trio, imaginatively named The Andrew London
Trio. He was previously Chief of swing trio Hot Club Sandwich, whose repertoire consisted mostly
of Andrew's whimsical, humourous and satirical ditties. He was also assistant Chief of Kapiti's
'Cattlestops', a five-piece country band whose Tui-nominated album 'Back to Rosetta Road'
provided much of the soundtrack to the movie 'Second Hand Wedding'.

“This was not a series of songs but a complete performance, and their banter and commentary was
a part of that. It was like sitting down with a group of friends reminiscing - such a cool relaxed vibe
- and then this great music kept being served up. Too Many Chiefs - Buy tickets. You won't regret it.

Following a huge run of international touring in the first half of the year, including appearances at Coachella, a North American Bubble Tour and a residency at London's Phonox, 1tbsp jumps the ditch with Bubble Tour - a live show that expands his ever-evolving world.

Across the last few years, 1tbsp, the Meanjin-born, Gadigal-based producer, songwriter, DJ and Dottidot label founder, has quietly assembled one of electronic music's most distinctive universes – a glossy, hyper-coloured landscape where reggaeton drums collide with toy-box synths, club music sparkles with pop sentiment, and every release feels like a portal into somewhere slightly unfamiliar.

Originally known through his Grammy-nominated alt-indie project Golden Vessel, Maxwell Byrne launched 1tbsp in 2021 as an outlet for stranger ideas. What began with the kanashī EP soon evolved into a fully realised creative universe, culminating in the release of his debut album Mosquito Love and later the acclaimed Megacity1000.

Released in 2024, Megacity1000 arrived like a transmission from a parallel metropolis - equal parts club record and pop experiment. Across the album's eight tracks, Byrne fused candy-coated percussion, shimmering vocal fragments and bright, maximalist production into a sound entirely his own. Support quickly followed from Pitchfork, Mixmag, CLASH, The Line of Best Fit and EARMILK, cementing 1tbsp as one of Australia's most forward-thinking electronic exports.

That same spirit extends beyond his own catalogue through Dottidot, Byrne's label and creative platform, which has become home to a growing network of artists and collaborators. Recent releases from label affiliates Soltera and Cherry Chola continue to expand the architecture of this ecosystem.

Now, for the first time, Bubble Tour arrives in Aotearoa this August, Saturday 22nd at Meow Nui.

KA RONGO KOE KI TE WAIATA O TE KŌIWI? Can you hear the song of the bone?

Supported by Creative NZ - Gigi Crayford under 'HINE' presents the debut EP ‘KA MUA KA MURI’ out 25th July. A musical journey tracing the threads of Whakapapa, exploring relationship to Atua, Pūrākau and the transformation of learning an ancestral tongue. Recorded on ancestrally affiliated land with full instrumentation by herself and her whānau, this project is drawn from deep wells of meaning and connection.

“GiGi’s soulful voice has an ancient quality, that feels whole and embodied. There is a depth that is rare and potent.” - Ariana Tikao, renowned practitioner and composer of taonga pūoro, and an established writer and poet.

“Mesmerising, theatrical and soulful reo” - Toni Huata - Former director of SOUNZ, Singer, Composer and legendary Māori performer

‘KA MUA KA MURI EP’ weaves Taonga Pūoro, sonic storytelling, poetry and Gigi's original folk noir style in both English and Te Reo Māori. A singer-songwriter on Autoharp, Guitar and Piano, Gigi is supported by brother Miles Crayford on Organ, father Greg Crayford on drums, Charlie Budd on Taonga Pūoro and Aslan Rowlands on Electric Guitar. Echoing the emotionally drenched lyricism of Joni Mitchell, enigmatic voice akin to Kate Bush & soaring ecstatic moments like Pink Floyd. Interwoven with Taonga Pūoro; creating a contemporary genre-bending experience. HINE reverberates with authentic expression, wahine power & the vital place music has in healing & self discovery.

With her maiden single release and successful show at MĀORILAND ŌTAKI in 2024 for’ KA MUA KA MURI’ HINE explored the grief of living in a matrix paved over matriarch world and the journey of remembering to return to the earth from a human-centric culture.

This tour releases the final 4 songs of the EP. Each an ode to a different Atua Māreikura, ranging from Papatūānuku, Hine Te Iwa Iwa, Murirangawhenua, Hine Moana, Hine Raukatauri & Hine Takurua.

Shows in Tāmaki Makaurau Auckland, Paekākāriki, Pōneke Wellington and Ōhinehou Lyttelton.

As a true sonic missionary, Nikau is creating a soothing “golden-era sound” as part of his mission to heal with his music. The songs of Casual Healing emphasise life lessons of aroha, peace and unity through powerful lyrical scribe woven into smooth reggae, soul rhythm. This infusion creates a unique nostalgic vibe, creating a captivating and comforting essence that evokes recollections of moments shared with friends and whānau. Having been handed a booklet of lyrics... we grab seats around the edge ... It’s all very casual, with the added delight of people dressed as sailors in striped tops and white hats, pirate hats and newspaper hats, and even life jackets! It’s like they know what is about to happen!

As the band takes to the stage... a spotlight falls upon storyteller Louis Tait. Microphone in hand he starts to weave a tale of the sea, to riffs of music from the band.

Back to those booklets of lyrics – this whole show is a singalong and it is with great enthusiasm that the first shanty begins...the audience sings and stomps and laughs.

What is it about shanties? They came out of shared singing and so they lend themselves to this, I guess. But what Vorn Dont le Père Etait Marin and Lake Davineer bring to these songs is a thoroughly modern, old-fashioned sense of fun and magic.

I am reserving specific comment for the currently most famous shanty in their repertoire, ‘The Wellerman’... The crowd goes wild! The stomping probably puts the hall onto Geonet. I would not have been surprised if a giant cracken had appeared and body-surfed the crowd.

long_description:
Four Islands, Infinite Interpretations.

New Music Islands explores how we can forge connections across vast geographies while also doing our own thing, here, in our own way. The evening will be presented in two halves. The first 45 minutes feature a New Music Islands programme showcasing selected works from the Faroe Islands, Aotearoa New Zealand, the Canary Islands and Gotland. The second half celebrates the richness and diversity of contemporary music in New Zealand with a selection of works by New Zealand composers.

The programme centres on four works that embrace openness through flexible instrumentation and deliberately broad performance instructions. Each ensemble is invited to make the music their own, resulting in unique interpretations as the programme travels between the four island communities.

Featuring performances by Tristan Carter, Jonny Marks, Erika Grant, Naoto Segawa and Rebecca Steel, with music by Jesse Austin-Stewart, Ruby Solly, Elliot Vaughan, Ciro Hernández, Lasse Thornin, Weston Olencki, Michelle Scullion, Jessie Leov, Garling Wu and Chris Cree Brown.

Each concert will be a singular experience, with this being the Aotearoa New Zealand presentation. - New Music Islands is an international collaboration between four member societies of the International Society for Contemporary Music (ISCM): the Faroe Islands Section, VICC (ISCM Gotland Section), COSIMITE (ISCM Affiliated Associate Member representing the Canary Islands) and CANZ (ISCM New Zealand Section).

name: The Broken Heartbreakers - Album Release Tour
long_description:
*Just announced, Eigenface will be joining in support at the Vogelhorn Bowling Club show!*

Ōtepoti’s longstanding indie folk favourites The Broken Heartbreakers have emerged from the mists to announce their brand new album, as well as a full nationwide tour this September. Imagine If We Could Just Keep Driving marks the band’s fifth album and debut on Nadia Reid’s boutique Slow Time Records label, set to be unveiled on July 17th.

FULL BAND ALBUM RELEASE TOUR - SEPTEMBER 2026

FRI 4 SEPT - GRAINSTORE GALLERY, OAMARU
SAT 5 SEPT - SPACE ACADEMY, CHRISTCHURCH
THURS 10 SEPT - WHAMMY, AUCKLAND
FRI 11 SEPT - ARTWORKS THEATRE, WAIHEKE
SAT 12 SEPT - VOGELMORN BOWLING CLUB, WELLINGTON
SAT 19 SEPT - HANOVER HALL, DUNEDIN

With the ballad of The Broken Heartbreakers harking back all the way to 2002, it’s clear that the band understand that the finer things in life take time. Their critically adored album How We Got To Now arrived over a decade ago in 2015, with a smattering of non-album singles and live appearances over the years keeping the band in the hearts and minds of their ever-loyal fanbase.

Now, after four years of writing and self-producing in their North East Valley, Dunedin home studio, founding members John Howell and Rachel Bailey return with The Broken Heartbreakers’ most fully realised record yet. Featuring exquisite cover art from Dudley Benson, and mixed by Aotearoa’s master of noise Nick Roughan (Skeptics, Dimmer) Imagine If We Could Just Keep Driving expands the band’s world brilliantly.

“Rachel and John are such gifted writers, observers, singers, and players,” says Slow Time Records founder Nadia Reid. “These songs are the stuff of life – life on life’s terms. They sound like Dunedin, and Ireland, like K’Road. I’m so grateful that this record is joining Slow Time’s stable of records.”

Music critic Graham Reid once described the band as having “a sound which draws equally on the Left Banke, the Everly Brothers, Brian Wilson, Beatles, alt-country harmonies and the Anglofolk tradition”. The Broken Heartbreakers’ music mixes the bleak with the beautiful, drawing on deep roots of folk and classic pop melody, but with a defiant, subversive twist and more than a touch of modern electricity.

Howell and Bailey’s new songs find them more defiant than ever, proudly redefining what a band known for having a wistful folky element can or should represent. Whilst The Broken Heartbreakers certainly enjoy plumbing “the broken hearted depths of personal despair and loss”, they also gleefully admit that their songs exist to take “well aimed barbs at the socioeconomic wasteland of the neoliberal era”.

With that said, it only seemed fitting for the band to come out swinging against the state of things with the album’s softly raging first single. Fuck You, Dangerous Age, bravely risking their press releases being caught by spam filters. Follow-up single What Is For You was a more dreamy and encouraging affair, inspired by a traditional Gaelic saying. Brand new single and opening track on the album How Long Is Too Long is a wintry song that will linger in your lungs for weeks.

To hear The Broken Heartbreakers on record is a special thing indeed, but to witness them live with a full band is a rare pleasure. This September, fans can hear these very special songs live in all their glory, with six shows spanning the motu. As well as the band’s core pair, the full touring band will feature drummer Paul McLennan-Kissel (who also performed powerfully and beautifully on the record), Ayumu Kobayashi on bass, and a mystery figure on keys and synths.

Don’t miss catching The Broken Heartbreakers on the Imagine If We Could Just Keep Driving album release tour; these magnificent stars may not align again for some time.

“beautiful, world-class music” - Victor Billot, Audioculture

STRUNG OUT (USA) RETURN FOR FULL-BLOWN NZ TOUR—PERFORMING Suburban Teenage Wasteland Blues IN FULL

Strung Out tore through NZ in 2023, and you lapped it up.

You loved them, and they loved you—so much so that they’re returning this September for a full-blown New Zealand tour, hitting four locations across both the North and South Island.

And this time, they’re bringing something special.

Marking the 30th anniversary of Suburban Teenage Wasteland Blues, the band are set to play the critically acclaimed, classic album in full. One of punk’s holy grails, it’s fast, ferocious, and precise—a record that helped define the genre and influenced generations of bands that followed.

Released in 1996, Suburban Teenage Wasteland Blues pushed the boundaries of the genre—faster, sharper, and more intricate than anything that came before.

Three decades on, it still hits hard, and hearing it played live, front to back, is an experience no self-respecting punk fan can miss.

Hailing from Simi Valley, California, Strung Out are long-standing punk rock royalty and one of Fat Wreck Chords’ defining “big four.” With decades of touring under their belts, they have a proven track record of igniting crowds and delivering high-octane, full-throttle punk shows.

Expect a night of relentless energy: razor-sharp riffs, pounding drums, and shout-along choruses delivered with force.

This is controlled chaos at its best: sweat-soaked rooms, ringing ears, and intensity that pulls you right in.

Last time Strung Out were here, shows sold out. This run will be no different.

long_description:
Doing the Most: A Pro-Trans Drag Fundraiser Show” is an opulent and over-the-top celebration of queer and trans resilience, featuring all-out performances from heavy hitters of the Wellington drag scene. Come for a night of extravagant and maximalist drag performances, knowing that the price of your ticket will have a direct, tangible impact on the safety and wellbeing of two members of our trans whānau.

About Nereida:

Nereida is a Black trans woman who came to NZ fleeing the violence in the United States. She spent years working tirelessly to support the Disabled community in Te-Whanganui-a-Tara (Wellington), whilst saving for gender affirming surgery, only to lose everything after racism, transphobia, and ongoing attacks on marginalised communities in Aotearoa impacted her job and therefore her visa.

During her time in Te Whagnanui-a-Tara, Nereida contributed to our queer and trans community by supporting local queer events, speaking out against anti-trans discrimination at organised protests and through her online platforms. She always invests so much of herself into every space she enters. Unfortunately, Nereida has been forced to leave Wellington; a long battle with workplace transphobia resulted in the loss of her sponsored work visa. Now, Nereida and her partner Lucien, a trans man, drag performer, and artist who has also been a vibrant contributor to Wellington’s local queer and activist spaces, are in Australia, isolated from the friendships and community they took years to build. Together, they are starting from scratch. They're trying to secure some safety by fulfilling the immigration requirements needed to stay in Australia. A key part of that safety is funding Nereida’s gender-affirming FFS surgery, which they have been saving and fundraising for with very little resources.

About the Event:

“Doing the Most: A Pro-Trans Drag Fundraiser Show” aims to draw together members of the local community to raise funds to help cover the financial costs of securing safety for Nereida and Lucien. All of the funds raised by this event will be given to Nereida and Lucien. It will be used to directly pay for Nereida’s gender affirming surgery, for the visa she needs to stay in Australia, and the travel costs for accessing the surgery.

Prepare for a night of opulent, outrageous, and over-the-top drag performances. Revel in the joy of being “too much” and refusing to shrink or “tone it down”, by coming dressed to the theme of “Doing the Most”, in whatever form that means for you! Prizes for best dressed awarded on the night!

long_description:
Following the release of their recent single, “I Do Mine”, Debt Club announce their first Aotearoa nationwide tour. The tour will celebrate the release of their debut album “Foothold” which is out August 12th & available for vinyl pre-order now!

Debt Club are a Pōneke based indie / folk rock six piece who blend jangling indie rock, folk, alt-country and emo into a sound defined by rich arrangements, soaring saxophone melodies, and emotionally direct songwriting. Since forming in 2023, the band has quickly become a notable presence in Aotearoa’s underground music scene through their dynamic live performances and textured, heartfelt songs. Debt Club have shared stages with Marlin's Dreaming, Phoebe Rings and Australia’s Floodlights, while appearing at festivals including Rhythm and Vines, Twisted Frequency, CubaDupa and Newtown Festival. Following the release of their debut EP, “Taste For Stout,” the band recently unveiled “I Do Mine,” the first single from their forthcoming debut album “Foothold,” due out on August 12th.

Joining Debt Club for the Wellington date is First Reserve & Dillon Jo!

First Reserve is inevitable. Before adopting the moniker in 2023, Ryan Connaghan had been prolifically writing music that communicated their experiences in life, love, and loneliness. These themes are all approached on songs like “Last One” and “Me & My Friends” – the first offerings from First Reserve’s debut EP “There’s A God” set for release on November 14th, 2025. Thanks to their exhilarating live performances joined by a four-piece band, First Reserve has amassed a cult of devoted supporters both in their hometown of Te Whanganui-a-Tara and beyond. On stage, their sound is both intimate and larger-than-life, combining influences from alt-rock, indie-folk, and pop. First Reserve has supported visiting internationals Hot Mulligan (US) and Keli Holiday (AUS), and have toured with Kiwi favourites PARK RD, There’s A Tuesday, and Wet Denim.

Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s staple, Dillon Jo, is a queer, female-fronted four-piece band formed at Massey University in Wellington. Describing their sound as “Dreamy Droppy Rock Pop,”. ‘Dillon Jo’ is the project of Wellington Based artists Betty Smith and Georgie Levien, building paths between the elements of dream pop, shoegaze, folk, alt rock, and indie pop to create their genre defying sound. They have discovered vibrant chemistry over the past few months since making quite a stir in Wellington, playing numerous shows including opening for The Rions, Foley, Wet Denim, Hemi Hemingway and Coast Arcade only to name a few. Having heard of each other through the Reality music TV show Take The Mic 2022 which they were both contestants on, they formed Dillon Jo in early 2025. Releasing their first acoustic single ‘It was you (she’s been waiting for)’ in April 2025 and releasing two more singles later in the year, including ‘Shiver’ and ‘Jo’. The band also consists of Kahu Sanson-Burnett, (a multi-talented musician, producer, and previous member of Parallel Park) and Ruadh Munro, (Drums and previous member of Scarlett crush) Dillon Jo has transformed their live sets into an unbridled big-sound shoegaze experience

long_description:
Mates on the road rolling out top quality songwriting and musicianship, with lashings of irony and
humour. - East Auckland Times
Three songwriters argue over headline billing, playing order, and whose shout it is, while talking
about themselves and playing their self-selected ’Greatest Hits’.
Wayne Mason is something of a Kiwi icon, having won the 'song of the Century' with his song
'Nature', first recorded in the '60s with The Fourmyula, and also covered by the Muttonbirds in the
'90s. Also a founder member of Rockinghorse and The Warratahs, Wayne now records and tours
under his own name. When on the road with the Chiefs his job is to deliver philosophical
profundities such as ‘music is like water - it just seeps away into the ground’.
Rob Joass is a 3 times Tui Award finalist, singer/songwriter and leader of folk/rock troubadours
Hobnail. His gritty songs are equal parts folk and country rock, with the occasional barb of satirical
humour betraying a cynical perspective on the human condition honed by decades of constant
touring through the highways and back roads Europe, Canada and NZ. Rob calls this ‘repeatedly
smashing myself up against a wall’.
Andrew London tours and records with his own trio, imaginatively named The Andrew London
Trio. He was previously Chief of swing trio Hot Club Sandwich, whose repertoire consisted mostly
of Andrew's whimsical, humourous and satirical ditties. He was also assistant Chief of Kapiti's
'Cattlestops', a five-piece country band whose Tui-nominated album 'Back to Rosetta Road'
provided much of the soundtrack to the movie 'Second Hand Wedding'.

“This was not a series of songs but a complete performance, and their banter and commentary was
a part of that. It was like sitting down with a group of friends reminiscing - such a cool relaxed vibe
- and then this great music kept being served up. Too Many Chiefs - Buy tickets. You won't regret it.

Aotearoa’s premier Bulgarian Folklore Vocal Ensemble, lead by Tui Mamaki, returns - offering a fresh collection of ancient melodies gathered on their recent trip to Bulgaria, with exquisite a capella arrangements, crafted for their unique blend of women’s voices.  

FULL CIRCLE is the culmination of an important year of mahi, which saw the ensemble travel to Bulgaria for the first time together, to perform at the famed Koprivshtitsa Festival and to study with some of the country's finest folklore keepers and vocalists.  This concert will be a presentation of livings songs, learnt in the living rooms, chitalishte (community halls), and on the mountain tops of Bulgaria.

Full Circle is the celebration of the completion of a journey to the source - a vibrant feminine tapestry of traditional Bulgarian song, where classic choral arrangements rub shoulders with rural treasures.  

We invite you to celebrate with us at Whanganui-a-Tara’s beautiful Saint Peters on Willis, where voices make the wood sing, on Sunday 20th September.

Be it through classic folklore choir arrangements or obscure rural treasure songs issue of Tui Mamaki’s long standing love affair with Bulgaria and its phenomenal voices, this ensemble explore that compelling vocal tone, that bewitchingly close harmony, those playful odd-meter rhythms and the colourful feminine fabric of a devoted community blend. Medena means “honeyed”.   

Featuring: Kate Bartlett, Julie Thompson, Lise Van Laere, Stephanie Frost, Caitlin Dale, Petra Murray, Abby Turbott, Jacqui Whall and Tui Mamaki.  

www.tuimamaki.com/medena-ensemble www.youtube.com/@MedenaEnsemble  

Highlight performances to date include: Koprivshtitsa Festival (Bulgaria) and Ellen Melville Centre 2025, Auckland Folk Festivals 2024-26, World Choir Games, VoCo and Unitarian Church, in collaboration with the Bulgarian Roses, 2024.

Very excited to play these shows! We will debut some new material as well - hope to see you there.

long_description:
Presented by The Slack Agency, Beloved Records, Remote Control Records:

This spring, Rowena Wise makes her long-awaited New Zealand debut, bringing an intimate solo show across the motu for the first time. With just voice and guitar, Rowena’s songs hit with a rare kind of clarity - tender, point-blank, and unafraid of the quietest truths.

From Melbourne to Auckland, Wellington to Oakura and beyond, the tour celebrates a body of work that holds space rather than demands attention, tracing heartbreak, estrangement, and the knottier growing pains of adulthood with candid poetic lyricism.

Since debuting in 2018, Rowena has amassed over 10 million streams, earned airplay across triple j, Double J and Unearthed, and toured extensively across Australia, the UK, Europe, the USA and Canada, supporting artists including Folk Bitch Trio, Holy Holy, Ball Park Music, Bernard Fanning and Paul Dempsey. Her 2024 debut album, Senseless Acts of Beauty, was praised by CLASH Magazine as “carefully etched indie folk” and shortlisted for the Australian Music Prize.
Expect favourites, new material, and the kind of stillness you can feel in your chest.

id: Papa M + Mick Turner | Wellington-Meow, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Papa M + Mick Turner | Wellington
long_description:
Two of the most distinctive guitarists in independent music come together for an intimate double bill this October.
﻿
Over the past four decades, David Pajo and Mick Turner have quietly shaped the sound of experimental rock, post-rock and instrumental music through an extraordinary body of work. Between them they've played in, recorded with or collaborated alongside artists including Slint, Dirty Three, Tortoise, Gang of Four, Cat Power, Interpol, Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bonnie 'Prince' Billy, Stereolab, Royal Trux and countless others, leaving an influence that reaches far beyond their own recordings.

Performing as Papa M, David Pajo has spent more than 25 years exploring the expressive possibilities of the electric guitar, moving effortlessly between shimmering instrumentals, folk songwriting and expansive, cinematic compositions. His latest album, Ballads of Harry Houdini, marks another bold chapter, weaving together intricate guitar work, textured electronics and vocals into what Drag City describes as a fresh, fine and fat-assed set of songs.

﻿As a founding member of Dirty Three, Mick Turner helped redefine instrumental rock, developing a guitar style that's instantly recognisable: lyrical, spacious and emotionally direct. Alongside his acclaimed solo recordings and work with Tren Brothers and Mess Esque, Turner has built a catalogue that rewards careful listening and continues to inspire musicians around the world.

﻿Twenty-six years after first touring Australia and New Zealand together, Papa M and Mick Turner reunite for a rare run of intimate performances. Whether you've followed their work for decades or are discovering it for the first time, this is a rare opportunity to experience two singular artists whose influence can be heard across generations of independent music.

Revisiting these moments from my musical life is something I am really looking forward to sharing.” Midge Ure

name: OvO (Italy) NZ Tour
long_description:
For many of us, music can be like a drug. At first everything and anything feels and is beyond amazing, but over time as our consumption increases, this magical euphoria wears off to a hollow and crushing emptiness. The now discerning music addict desperately searches for that new thing that will make them feel the high that they once had. But it gets harder to again feel this way. Until they stumble across something so unique, original, and idiosyncratic they cannot help but feel giddy, childish excitement.

OvO are one of those bands. Curiously infuriating yet dangerously exhilarating in their inability to be pigeon hold into genre or specific sound. Deftly navigating between noise rock, doom, extreme and blackened metal, industrial sludge and even electronica. “Decibel Magazine” have perhaps described them best by hailing the bands sound as “a David Lynch dance party”. Italy’s OvO, continue to rewrite the definition of what alternative music can be. Something which New Zealand audiences can look forward to seeing this October 2026.


Formed by Stefania Pedretti and Bruno Dorella in Milan, Italy in the late 90s. OvO have taken their inspiration from the likes of Suicide, Swans, and Diamana Galas. Centred around the ear piercing banshee-like vocals of Stefania, and a constant guitar drone and dark menace as the undercurrent of their songs. Bruno, equally essential in their music, pounds a stripped down drum-set as if he were the leader of an invading war party. Coupled with intensive percussion samples to help craft a unique and experimental sound.


With 25 years as a band, 11 albums behind them (including their most recent Gemma), over 1000 shows/festivals across the globe, and sharing stages with many of the biggest names in experimental music; Godflesh, Lightning Bolt, Thurston Moore, Sleepytime Gorilla Music, Psychic TV, Dillinger Escape Plan, Big Brave, Ufomammut, among others - New Zealand audiences have their chance to see one of the most unique and experienced bands still active.

long_description:
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.
﻿
Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.

﻿More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.

﻿When it comes to grunge, or even just Seattle, I think there was one band that made the definitive music of the time. It wasn't us or Nirvana, but Mudhoney. Nirvana delivered it to the world, but Mudhoney were the band of that time and sound. – Eddie Vedder (Pearl Jam)

﻿A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.

id: Anthonie Tonnon Presents Cinematographer-Hannah Playhouse, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Anthonie Tonnon Presents Cinematographer
long_description:
Taite Music Prize-winning songwriter Anthonie Tonnon presents his immersive new live show, Cinematographer.

Three years in the making, Cinematographer combines live electronic music, cinematic storytelling and visual design into an immersive performance. Featuring visual DJing by Erica Sklenars, videography by Theo Taylor, styling by Karlya Smith and design by Daniel Alexander, the show sees Tonnon playing the roles of DJ, singer, documentarian and revolutionary lecturer.

The show explores two timelines: the Situationist International in France and Italy during the 1960s, and Whanganui, New Zealand at the turn of the millennium - a mysterious, forgotten city where a new battle is being waged against what Guy Debord famously called The Society of the Spectacle.

Swapping his guitar for a vocoder, and transforming two Synthstrom Deluges into honorary turntables, Tonnon connects these seemingly distant worlds through the musical language of turn-of-the-millennium dance culture.

Cinematographer is part film, part francophile performance lecture, part disco club set, says Tonnon. It's a world that we've built for this new music, exploring some newfound passions – the French avant-garde, cinema, urban politics of the 1960s, turn-of-the-millennium dance culture and documentary films, and the glorious, mystifying city of Whanganui.

The ambitious audiovisual performance introduces an entirely new body of work developed with Tonnon's band and longtime producer Jonathan Pearce. The new single and video Executive Assistant offers the first glimpse into this new world - Tonnon's first new music in three years.

Doors open: 8.45PM I Show 9:15PM

Unallocated seating and standing available.

Early Bird tickets available until Monday 10 August or until allocation sells out.

This summer, Cat Power returns to New Zealand for a run of special shows performing her seminal 2006 album The Greatest in full, alongside songs spanning one of the most singular catalogues in contemporary music.

Recorded in Memphis with members of the legendary Hi Rhythm section, The Greatest remains a defining statement from Marshall: smoky, soulful and heartbreakingly intimate. Featuring enduring tracks including “The Greatest”, “Living Proof” and “Lived in Bars”, the album cemented Cat Power as one of the most influential voices of her generation.

To mark the album’s 20th anniversary, these rare performances will revisit the record front to back, a chance to experience its quiet power, emotional depth and timeless beauty in the live setting it deserves.

Support for these shows will be Lawrence Arabia - the acclaimed musical project of Christchurch-born singer-songwriter James Milne, one of New Zealand’s most celebrated and influential contemporary artists. Across a career spanning nearly two decades, Milne has released a string of critically acclaimed albums, earning an APRA Silver Scroll for his song Apple Pie Bed, the inaugural Taite Music Prize, and multiple Aotearoa Music Awards.

There are few artists who can hold a room the way Cat Power can. Experience the magic of The Greatest and re-enter the orbit of the early millennium in these raw, hypnotic shows in November.
